gen-flavors-gf-fanwood-text: Stubby, cheerful, built like a carpenter's pencil. Flavors holds every stroke to a cable-like thickness, while Fanwood Text lets its curves swell slightly heavier than the joins, with a large-eyed, bookish lowercase.
gen-flavors-gf-holtwood-one-sc: Round bowls with walls that never swell or taper. Flavors draws that unwavering line up top, while Holtwood One SC runs low and wide-tracked below, its serif curves nearly closing.
gen-flavors-gf-manuale: Flavors puts a single flat line weight through every glyph, with towering lowercase and diagonals as heavy as its stems. Manuale, a serif, shifts its stroke weight noticeably but never dramatically.
gen-flavors-gf-noto-naskh-arabic: Whimsical but bossy, like outlines drawn in one width. Noto Naskh Arabic, a text serif, adds the slight heft change of a stone-carved inscription, so a larger heading over a smaller body would suit it.
gen-flavors-gf-noto-nastaliq-urdu: Drawn with a ruler and compass, then given swagger. Flavors keeps its lines unwavering and chunky, while Noto Nastaliq Urdu, a classic serif, thins its bowls slightly at the sides and keeps a tight vertical rhythm.
gen-flavors-gf-noto-rashi-hebrew: Flavors gives its o equally thick sides and top, and the lowercase towers like a stubby pencil stroke. Noto Rashi Hebrew, a serif, follows with a modest weight change in its round letters, like lightly engraved brass.
gen-flavors-gf-noto-serif-ahom: Chunky, hairline-free and a bit cheeky. Noto Serif Ahom, a text serif, brings the gentle thick-thin shift of a soft pencil, and its joins taper without ever vanishing.
gen-flavors-gf-noto-serif-armenian: Flavors cuts every stroke to one width, with diagonals as hefty as the stems. Noto Serif Armenian, a text serif, gives a long page a modest thick-and-thin rhythm across each word, with big open counters.
gen-flavors-gf-noto-serif-balinese: Lines that hold their thickness, topped by a pencil-stub lowercase. Noto Serif Balinese, a serif, sits between flat and dramatic strokes, so the two feel like a sturdy sign beside a gentle page.
gen-flavors-gf-noto-serif-bengali: Flavors strokes run contrast-free from stem to terminal, whimsical yet commanding. And Noto Serif Bengali, a classic serif, keeps a mild, approachable contrast with slightly thinner hairlines, which makes a longer passage go down easily.
